newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close up but off mid-session highs.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close up but off mid-session highs.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed higher on Monday but profit-taking by speculators trimmed early gains, brokers said.
The Delhi bourse's benchmark index closed 11.90 points higher at 823.73 points. The index had spurted to 832.63 points at mid-session.
Traders said the rally in share prices, fuelled by foreign institutional investors' (FIIs) buying, was cut short by speculators and domestic mutual funds as they unloaded positions at higher levels.

"Hectic activity in multi-national companies' shares was the main feature of the session as FIIs indulged in building up huge positions in anticipation of a further upsurge in their prices," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Services.
"Mostly the buying was triggered by a hike in FII investment from 24 to 30 percent," Malhotra added.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday hiked the investment limit in firms for foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to 30 percent from 24 percent in the budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April 1.
Brokers cautioned the rally could be short-lived.
"Though the sentiment seems to be bullish the market should witness some technical correction in prices soon," said another broker.
Hindustan Lever surged 32 rupees, or 3.27 percent, to 1,010 rupees on FII buying, brokers said. The share surged to 1,050.25 before dipping again.
Brooke Bond Lipton India gained 15 rupees to 420.
Nestle India rose 11 rupees, or 4.3 percent, to 267.
Reliance Industries dropped 3.45 rupees to 307.45 on profit-taking by speculators.
State Bank of India dropped 4.90 rupees to 326.10.
